harness_notes: vector_layer_of_record is 'maximumWaterExtentA', the newer EMS layer-naming convention — same cumulative-maximum-extent role as emsr773/emsr692's 'maximumFloodExtentA', confirmed via the EMS dashboard-api's per-product layer listing, not assumed from the name alone.
Reference product is ~3 days post the 2023-10-07 event peak (Storm Babet) — not a peak-state comparison, same caveat class as Paiporta/Kanalia.
Reference geometry is the FULL River Spey AOI delineation, clipped to Insh's town boundary at scoring time — no separately-published village-level EMS product exists.

No permanent-water mask available for this AOI in this pass — the River Spey/Insh Marshes floodplain has real permanent wetland/marsh water bodies, so (like Kanalia's Lake Karla) 'permanent water' vs 'flood' is somewhat blurred here too, though less extreme than Kanalia's drained-lake case.

An earlier product (DEL_PRODUCT, 2023-10-08, closer to peak) exists for this AOI but does not carry a maximumWaterExtentA layer (only observedEventA/waterDepthA) — DEL_MONIT01 is the earliest available product with the layer this harness's reference_loader expects.
Pipeline completed but produced zero hazard zones — IoU/precision/recall against the EMS reference are undefined (0/0), not a score of 0.
